compounding_issues: Session 1 discarded the seeded app.py (Flask auth API) wholesale and never deleted it, leaving a dead file in the tree across all 5 sessions with zero continuity from the seed

Session 4's transport refactor is half-finished: _create_transport reads the TRANSPORT env var but ignores it (always returns WebSocketTransport), and the superseded ClientRegistry class remains as dead code at server.py:287

Session 5's rate limiting is Redis-only — is_rate_limited returns False when REDIS_URL is unset, so the headline cross-cutting feature silently no-ops in the default single-node deployment that sessions 1-3 established
Rate limit enforcement in ws_handler only covers the general broadcast branch; subscribe/unsubscribe messages bypass the limit entirely
key_decisions: Greenfield rewrite in session 1: replaced the seeded Flask auth API with an asyncio/aiohttp + websockets real-time notification server
Channel-based pub/sub semantics (ChannelManager with subscribe/unsubscribe) as the core messaging model in session 2
SQLite MessageStore plus optional Redis pub/sub broker in session 3 for persistence and multi-node fan-out, driven by env-var config
Transport abstraction (BaseTransport ABC / WebSocketTransport) in session 4 to centralize connection management away from ClientRegistry
Cross-cutting hardening in session 5: Redis rate limiting, MESSAGE_TTL_DAYS expiry with a background cleanup task, and a paginated /history endpoint with has_more
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across a logical arc: session 1 built a clean minimal broadcast MVP, session 2 added a coherent channel abstraction, session 3 layered on persistence and Redis integration, session 4 performed a structural refactor toward a transport abstraction (slightly incomplete, leaving dead code), and session 5 delivered production-oriented hardening (rate limits, TTL cleanup, history). Sessions 2-3 and 3-5 build directly on prior infrastructure, and the final state passes 72 tests, so the overall arc is upward despite the refactor session's unfinished edges.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent 5-session progression from a broadcast MVP to a hardened, persistent, channel-based notification service, marred mainly by a seed-app disconnect and a session 4 refactor that introduced but never finished a transport abstraction.
